title: improv·artist · patterned (Bridget Riley)
mutation_directive: improv artist: patterned via Bridget Riley

improv_extras.practice: op-art; black-and-white waves and dot-fields that pulse on the retina

v1.feedback: Strong Riley translation — the triple-wave interference producing moiré-like banding is faithful to 'Movement in Squares' and 'Fall', and the charcoal-to-bone palette with umber warmth is well-restrained. The scale compression in wave troughs is a nice touch that sells the op-art spatial illusion. Two refinements: the wave speeds (0.18, 0.12, 0.07) could be even slower — Riley's paintings are static, so the motion should feel glacial, almost imperceptible, like staring until the painting moves itself. Consider adding a fourth wave at a slightly off-axis angle to create more complex interference nodes — right now the banding reads as mostly horizontal stripes rather than the full-field perceptual dazzle Riley achieves.

v2.feedback: Strong Riley translation — four-wave interference with scale-compression in troughs captures her spatial-illusion language well, and the ortho camera is the correct framing for a retinal-pulse grid. Two refinements: (1) the leaf/lozenge shape softens the optical punch Riley gets from hard-edged circles or squares — try a flat disc or rounded-rect with crisp boundaries so the moiré interference reads more sharply at a glance; (2) the umber mid-tone warmth is tasteful but dilutes the black-white contrast that makes Riley's fields vibrate — consider dropping it to 0.06–0.08 weight or reserving it for the vignette edge only, letting the centre stay high-contrast charcoal↔bone.
